$comment: Conformance traceability manifest (#245). Each requirement row maps one normative clause (or one facet of a multi-part clause) to its observable conformance assertion and the tests that drive it. Validated by scripts/check-conformance-manifest.mjs: unknown anchors, quoted clauses missing from their anchored section, duplicate IDs, missing tests, and coverage states inconsistent with their mappings all fail CI; rows not fully tested are the visible outstanding report, never silent. observation.local records this implementation's chosen behavior where the spec permits more than one; a local pin never becomes the protocol requirement. Rows whose applicability names a capability apply only where the deployment claims it: a runner MUST NOT mark an unclaimed capability nonconforming, and a failed SHOULD row is a recorded departure, not a hard fail. source.specs names, for every spec file a row references, the revision (the commit whose text that spec's rows were validated against) and content_sha256 (a mechanical gate recomputed from the working-tree file's current bytes, which must match, or the entry needs deliberate re-review and a bump before CI passes again); the stale-text check catches an edited or relocated clause inside an anchored section, source.specs catches any other edit to a spec whose rows were not re-reviewed. Completeness provenance per spec lives in the tracking issues, not in this manifest. Each row's profiles array (enumerated at the top level in profiles) names which published baseline profile(s) this requirement belongs to: a floor document beyond core typically carries only runtime-enforced, core typically carries both, and an empty array means this requirement belongs to no published baseline profile, whether because its document sits outside every baseline or because a baseline document's own row is scoped to an optional capability no published baseline selects; profiles and applicability are orthogonal, since applicability already encodes election of an OPTIONAL capability.

requirements.notes: MissionSignalEmitter gates delivery on the receiver-declared `mission_capabilities_supported`: an event whose effective-authority change is represented by `authority_changed` ALONE is withheld from an undeclared stream. The gate keys on a `containment_version` ADVANCE rather than its presence, tracked per Mission with the same cursor discipline the receiver uses, so the composite case is caught: a discharge on a PREVIOUSLY CONTAINED Mission carries containment_version unchanged and is still gated, while the contain commit before it (an actual advance) still reaches the undeclared stream, leaving containment's delivery rules unchanged. With no cursor yet, only containment_version 1 counts as an advance; a higher first-seen value is ambiguous and the gate withholds. The Stream Configuration object itself is not modeled (no SSF stream-management endpoints exist here): the declaration is a registered consumer's property on the emitter.

observation.normative: evaluate() (step 4b) narrows a joined delegate's effective authority to entries carrying a join_delegation member whose allowed_delegates (when present) names that client; BOTH the deployment's DelegatePolicy.maxDepth ceiling AND each entry's own join_delegation.max_depth are compared against context.mission_join.delegate_depth, a REQUEST fact the PEP resolves fresh and carries onto the decision request (PepDeps.masJoin.resolveDelegateDepth), never a token act chain and never looked up by the PDP from static configuration (#557 review points 1, 3). The depth source is the deployment's own actor records (ActorRecords, services/mcp-payments/src/actor-records.ts): records are keyed on the canonical (issuer, id) pair, and resolveDepth walks delegated_by toward the Mission's own client_id (depth 0, adding 1 per hop), resolving ABSENT for no record, an unrooted chain, a cycle, or a chain that never reaches the Mission's client. An absent depth denies unconditionally on the delegate disposition, including where no max_depth is declared anywhere, per rule 5's own sentence: "A delegate with no actor record under the Mission is not recorded as acting under it, and the join fails `mission_mismatch`." The hook the PEP resolves depth through takes the canonical (issuer, id) reference and the Mission's own client_id, both facts of the request the PEP already holds, so the ledger's resolver satisfies it with no issuer bound at construction: a record appended under one issuer is never consumed for a same-id Mission from another (#557 stage C2). requirements.text: A permit under a join never exceeds any of three independently evaluated bounds: the authority the acting credential itself carries (the token as issued, enforced at the Resource Server or gateway), the Mission's approved authority, and current Resource policy.

observation.normative: each of the three bounds denies ON ITS OWN with the other two satisfied, and all three satisfied permits, which is what makes them independently evaluated rather than one check wearing three names. Bound 1 is the acting credential's own authority (PepDeps.masJoin.resolveOrdinaryAuthority), intersected against the joined Mission authority by resource+action before the PDP runs; absent, it cannot be honestly evaluated, so the joined route fails closed with out_of_authority rather than treating an unconfigured bound as unbounded. Bound 2 is the Mission's approved authority, matched by evaluate() against the joined authority set. Bound 3 is current Resource policy, the existing fga.checkWithContext call, which denies out_of_authority with both other bounds satisfied. The demo supplies a real bound-1 evaluator (src/demo/src/stack.ts): the credential's verified scope claim mapped through config/mas-join.json's scope_actions, so it models the token AS ISSUED and a narrower token yields a narrower permit for the same client
observation.local: bound 3's independence is shown by evaluation, not by an independent policy SOURCE: the contextual tuples the FGA check runs against are themselves derived from the matched Mission authority entry's own constraints (policy-view.ts, 'authority + constraint -> ephemeral grant'). A deployment whose resource policy is authored separately from the Mission would exercise the same call with a genuinely independent input; this one does not, and the row does not claim it does

requirements.notes: #557 review point 4, ruled: promote distinguishability normative (rule 9), leave the digest construction unfixed (only one implementation exists; freezing it now would make a later correction a breaking change to evidence joins). The first two cited tests together prove the row's actual clause -- a SEPARATE-MEMBER claim, not a same-response value-inequality claim: join_view_id is truthy on a joined permit and undefined on a non-joined one, so presence/absence alone already separates joined evidence from direct evidence, which is exactly the defect the review identified (a joined decision's policy_view_id alone cannot be told apart from a direct decision's). NOT asserted: the anchor's TOCTOU-at-time-of-use clause -- reverifying the SAME single permitted attempt via Pep.reverify() immediately before execution, the way parameter-binding.must-bind-and-reverify does for an ordinary permit. That path is not reachable through any public server API for an approval-gated action: callWriteTool/callTransactionTool take no actionApproval parameter (only Pep.enforce() does, and it has no execution step of its own), and Pep.reverify() itself has no approval parameter at all -- it only re-checks the generic parameter_digest, with no notion of the approval object. The cited tests prove an unrecognized type and an absent type member both deny unsupported_authorization_type rather than pass through or misclassify as out_of_authority, a side-by-side case contrasting the two denial reasons on otherwise-identical requests, a mixed-authority_set case (an unrecognized-type entry alongside a valid entry for the same resource/actions) proving the unrecognized entry is skipped rather than short-circuiting the match (skip-not-shortcircuit unaffected by the classification fix), and a positive control (same file) proving the recognized-type case still permits. requirements.notes: list_invoices is the bulk/cross-vendor material read (#610 GAP 1, hardened by #612 finding 1): a requested vendor_id binds through the ordinary vendor-constraint check (out-of-scope -> out_of_authority; in-scope -> permitted, bound to exactly that vendor); its absence binds the result set to the entry's own vendor scope (proven for a two-vendor allowlist, not just a singleton) rather than the unconstrained store. Result-set filtering alone is not Runtime parameter binding: list_invoices now derives a normalized list Operation Profile ({action, resource, vendor_scope, vendor_scope_source}, effective-params.ts's buildListEffectiveParams/deriveVendorScope in pep.ts), a genuine parameter_digest enters the PDP request and the retained Decision Evidence (previously absent entirely), and server.ts's callReadTool reverifies that digest against a freshly loaded MissionView immediately before execution (Pep.reverifyList), exactly as the write/transaction paths already do. The omitted-vendor_id normal form is a THIRD, explicit case (vendor_scope_source: "all"), never collapsed with an entry's own allowlist even when the two enumerate the same vendors (proven by a distinct-digest test). This row's role is AS (the draft's generic "Deployments MUST" language); this deployment has no separate AS-side gate for read parameter binding, so the PEP is where the requirement is enforced and tested. #612 finding 3 fix: the FGA/PDP request now names the FULL collection (resource.properties.vendor_ids, populated in pep.ts's bindsVendorScope "entry" branch), and evaluateInner's step 6a checks every named member independently, denying the WHOLE read out_of_authority the moment any one member is refused (fail-closed choice: the response contract has no lane for a partially narrowed permit). Proven with a stub Fga (denies one specific vendor object) at both the pure evaluateInner level and the full pep.ts->server.ts integration level, since this domain model's contextual-tuple-only grant mechanism has no way to make a LIVE OpenFGA check independently disagree with the Mission's own allowlist. There is still no genuine persisted Resource-policy layer distinct from the Mission's authority_set in this deployment (a `resource_policy` denial reason is named in the draft's failure classification but implemented nowhere here), so the stub proves the MECHANISM (every named member is actually checked) rather than a real independent policy disagreement. entry_digest still anchors only the Mission ceiling; it was never evidence of Resource-policy's independent say and still is not.

requirements.notes: Before #610's fix, list_invoices without vendor_id was never actually classified as materially unaffecting the resource set in the sense of successfully returning everything: a vendor-constrained entry always denied out_of_authority (the unbound call's implicit vendorId of "" never matched a real vendors constraint) and an unconstrained entry threw an FGA validation error (the default resourceObj named an FGA object type/id the domain model does not accept). Neither path reached a permit, so the pre-fix behavior was closer to broken-and-fail-closed-by-accident than to the issue's literal "returns every invoice" description; the LATENT misclassification was in server.ts's execute(), which would have trusted args.vendor_id blindly and returned the unfiltered store had a permit ever been reached. The fix repairs the underlying FGA object typing (so the call reaches a real decision at all) and binds the result: a vendor-constrained entry narrows the bulk result to its own multi-vendor scope, never the whole store (proven for two vendors, with a third excluded, not just a singleton); an unconstrained entry legitimately keeps returning every vendor, which is the entry's true scope, not a misclassification. Verified this fix is reached from every entry point: McpPaymentsServer.callReadTool directly, and both mcp-transport.ts's and mcp-http-transport.ts's route() functions fall through to callReadTool for list_invoices (no separate switch bypasses it). This row's role is AS for the same reason noted on the paired must-require-binding-for-material-reads row; see that row's notes for the representative-vendor FGA-check limitation, which applies equally here. #612 finding 1 hardening: the bulk read's normalized parameters (vendor_scope/vendor_scope_source) now actually enter parameter_digest and are reverified immediately before execution (Pep.reverifyList), so a Mission-authority change landing between the permit and execution is caught as a digest mismatch rather than executed on a stale scope (proven with a live-OpenFGA TOCTOU test that narrows the entry's vendors constraint via the same beforeReverify test-hook idiom callWriteTool already uses for writes). #612 finding 3 fix: the FGA/PDP request now names the FULL collection (resource.properties.vendor_ids, populated in pep.ts's bindsVendorScope "entry" branch), and evaluateInner's step 6a checks every named member independently, denying the WHOLE read out_of_authority the moment any one member is refused (fail-closed choice: the response contract has no lane for a partially narrowed permit). Proven with a stub Fga (denies one specific vendor object) at both the pure evaluateInner level and the full pep.ts->server.ts integration level, since this domain model's contextual-tuple-only grant mechanism has no way to make a LIVE OpenFGA check independently disagree with the Mission's own allowlist. There is still no genuine persisted Resource-policy layer distinct from the Mission's authority_set in this deployment (a `resource_policy` denial reason is named in the draft's failure classification but implemented nowhere here), so the stub proves the MECHANISM (every named member is actually checked) rather than a real independent policy disagreement. entry_digest still anchors only the Mission ceiling; it was never evidence of Resource-policy's independent say and still is not.

tests.name: M6 ARAP reevaluate (scenario 5) > denies requestable, resolves via ARS approval, re-evaluates to a permit -- no token issued

observation.normative: a PDP response under this profile never carries executable residual policy; decisions and instructions are the only response forms

requirements.text: REQUIRED, and equal to the request's `action.properties.parameter_digest`, when the action was parameter-bound. The PEP MUST enforce the exact request binding.

observation.normative: a parameter-bound permit's conditions.parameter_digest equals the request's supplied digest, and the executing PEP enforces exactly that binding

The PEP's enforcement of the exact binding is proven by the reverification tests: server.ts's callReadTool/callWriteTool/callTransactionTool all read the digest from decision.context.conditions.parameter_digest and recompute-and-compare against authoritative state immediately before execution, refusing parameter_mismatch on any divergence (proven for both the write path, pre-existing, and the list-read path, #612 finding 1). Known limitation, unrelated to this row's PEP-enforcement text: the request-side carriage this profile's current examples show (action.properties.parameter_digest) differs from this deployment's context.parameter_digest placement; that request-shape divergence is pre-existing and out of this finding's scope (response-context only), flagged here rather than silently carried.

requirements.text: `valid_until` MUST NOT exceed:

observation.normative: a permit's conditions always carries valid_until (an RFC 3339 timestamp, REQUIRED), and its value never exceeds the minimum of the credential's expiry, any satisfied approval's approved_until, the state valid-through, and any policy-defined maximum lifetime for the class

requirements.text: The PDP MUST set `use_limit: 1` for a permit in the high-consequence classes ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime}}), and the PEP MUST treat a high-consequence permit lacking it as invalid.

observation.normative: every high-consequence-class permit carries use_limit: 1, and the PEP refuses a high-consequence permit lacking it, applying its own classification floor independent of the PDP's internal class label

requirements.notes: #612 finding 2 downgrades this row honestly: it was marked tested against transaction.test.ts's scenario 4, which proves the transaction tier executes a wire transfer exactly once through the hard-coded redemption/lease/consumption state machine, but never reads or asserts on conditions.use_limit (or the prior flat single_use) at all; that test is not probative for this row's wire-shape text. The value-level bug this migration also fixes: evaluate.ts previously set single_use only for action_class === "irreversible_action", so a send_remittance_email (external_commitment, also a high-consequence class per runtime#classification) permit never carried a use limit. The PDP half is now directly tested for BOTH high-consequence classes present in this deployment (irreversible_action, external_commitment; privileged_administration is unused). The PEP-side half of this row's text ("the PEP MUST treat a high-consequence permit lacking it as invalid ... applying its own deployment classification floor independent of the PDP's internal class label") is NOT implemented anywhere in this deployment: server.ts's transaction-tier single-use redemption is unconditional on the tool identity, never gated on reading conditions.use_limit and comparing it against the PEP's own floor. Partial, not tested, until that PEP-side floor check exists.

requirements.text: A permit carrying a condition member the PEP does not recognize is invalid: the PEP MUST NOT release the action's effect under it.

observation.normative: a permit whose conditions include a member the PEP does not recognize is treated as invalid, and the PEP does not release the action's effect under it

Scoped correctly to conditions members only (a companion test proves an unknown TOP-LEVEL member, outside conditions, does not trigger this rule).

requirements.text: on a permit the PEP MUST fulfill each obligation before releasing the action's effect; on a denial the PEP MUST still deny the action and MUST additionally execute every returned obligation. observation.normative: the PEP fulfills every attached obligation before releasing a permitted action's effect and treats an unfulfilled or unrecognized one as an effective deny; on a denial the PEP still denies and additionally executes every returned obligation

requirements.text: The PEP MUST achieve the required context before releasing the action's effect, and the original permit continues.

requirements.text: an obligation MUST NOT be marked optional or downgraded to advice, and permit request binding, permit expiry, use limits, evidence emission, step-up, and mandatory notification are never advice.

requirements.text: Every runtime failure condition, whether named in the runtime profile's failure-mode table or in its other normative requirements ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime}}), surfaces through exactly one of four carriers in this binding: a Refusal Record for a PEP or PDP refusal before any PDP decision ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence}}), a PDP denial (`reason` in the decision context, `denial_reason` in Decision Evidence), a permit obligation ({{obligations}}), or an Execution Evidence `error` for a failure after a permit

observation.normative: every runtime-profile failure condition maps to exactly one of the four evidence/response carriers this binding defines; none is left uncarried and none is carried by more than one

requirements.text: The requesting component and the executing PEP MUST be the same enforcement identity, on the same mutually authenticated channel that requested the permit. A permit is valid only on that channel and identity, and MUST NOT be relayed to another component as a bearer grant.

observation.normative: a permit is valid only for the same enforcement identity, on the same mutually authenticated channel, that requested it, and is never relayed to another component as a bearer grant

requirements.text: Signed Decision Evidence ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence}}) MUST NOT be accepted as authorization to act: it is retrospective evidence of what the PDP decided, never a live credential a distinct component presents to execute.

observation.normative: signed Decision Evidence is never accepted as authorization to act; it is retrospective evidence, not a live executable credential

requirements.text: A PEP permit cache MUST key on the request's cache key ({{projections}}), which already excludes observation telemetry by definition, so a per-request timestamp cannot prevent a cache hit.

observation.normative: a PEP permit cache keys on the canonical cache key (the authorization binding plus state generation, excluding observation telemetry), so a cached permit is never reused for a request whose cache key differs

requirements.text: The PEP SHOULD propagate the permit's `evaluation_id` to the resource request in the `Mission-Decision` request header field

observation.normative: the PEP propagates the permit's evaluation_id to the resource request in the Mission-Decision header, so a Resource Server that logs it joins its access log to the decision that permitted it

requirements.text: where the deployment signs resource requests the signature MUST cover it.

observation.normative: where a deployment signs resource requests, the signature covers the Mission-Decision header carrying evaluation_id

requirements.text: a Resource Server MUST NOT treat it as a permit; the permit-binding rules above govern.

observation.normative: the Mission-Decision header's evaluation_id is a correlation aid only; a Resource Server never treats its presence or value as a permit

requirements.text: independent of anything the PDP returns, a PEP that claims Runtime Evidence MUST emit one Execution Evidence Object ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence}}) for the final disposition of every consequential permit: `completed`, `failed`, or `suppressed` before release.

observation.normative: a PEP claiming the Runtime Evidence profile emits exactly one Execution Evidence Object per consequential permit, keyed on the stable execution_id, for every completed/failed/suppressed disposition; this requirement is meaningful only where the deployment also claims Transaction Assurance for the class, since that profile is what makes execution outcome reverification and single-use disposition tracking load-bearing (runtime.transaction-assurance-tier)

tests.name: M5 transaction-assurance tier > scenario 4: wire transfer executes once with permit, evidence, and reconciliation

requirements.text: The PEP MUST record the emission failure durably and surface it on its operational alarm path

observation.normative: if Execution Evidence emission fails after an irreversible effect, the PEP durably records the emission failure and surfaces it on its operational alarm path rather than retroactively altering the effect. Applies only to a PEP claiming Runtime Evidence; meaningful chiefly where the class also claims Transaction Assurance (runtime.transaction-assurance-tier), since that is what makes the recorded execution outcome load-bearing.

requirements.text: the PEP MUST durably reserve evidence capacity for the execution, an evidence reservation, before acting, and MUST fail closed when the reservation cannot be made.

observation.normative: where transaction assurance depends on later evidence, the PEP durably reserves evidence capacity before acting and fails closed when it cannot make the reservation. Applies only to a PEP claiming Runtime Evidence, and is load-bearing precisely when the deployment also claims Transaction Assurance for the class (runtime.transaction-assurance-tier), since that is what makes later evidence a precondition for the execution's own assurance claim.

requirements.text: when the bound elapses without a confirming event the PEP MUST refresh from a Mission state source rather than continue on the cache.

observation.normative: in event_driven mode, once the staleness bound elapses without a confirming invalidation event, the PEP refreshes from a Mission state source rather than continuing to rely on cached state

requirements.text: A PEP conforming to the Decision Base MUST:

observation.normative: a conforming PEP carries validated-token-only decision inputs matched on resource.properties.audience, supplies parameter_digest where required, processes obligations correctly, honors every decision condition under its own classification floor, keeps requesting and executing identity the same, and keys permit caches on the cache key; Execution Evidence and Refusal Record emission are Runtime Evidence profile duties, not Decision Base ones (#703)

requirements.text: A PEP additionally claiming the Runtime Evidence profile ({{profiles-and-capabilities}}) MUST emit a Refusal Record ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence}}) for a pre-decision refusal, and, for the classes the runtime profile's transaction-assurance tier covers, an Execution Evidence Object for the final disposition of every consequential permit

observation.normative: a PEP claiming the Runtime Evidence profile emits a Refusal Record for every pre-decision refusal and, for transaction-assurance-tier classes, an Execution Evidence Object for the final disposition of every consequential permit; a PEP claiming only the Decision Base is not required to (#703, closing the unconditional-adoption-gate defect #703 identified)

requirements.text: A PDP conforming to the Decision Base MUST:

observation.normative: a conforming PDP refuses an in-scope request lacking Mission decision context and performs the consistency checks, classifies every denial per the runtime-denial-classification, returns the full decision context, and advertises the mission-runtime capability URN; emitting the runtime evidence companion's records is a Runtime Evidence profile duty, not a Decision Base one (#703)

requirements.text: A PDP additionally claiming the Runtime Evidence profile ({{profiles-and-capabilities}}) MUST emit the records of {{I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-runtime-evidence}} for every decision, and a Refusal Record for an in-scope request it refuses before evaluation

observation.normative: a PDP claiming the Runtime Evidence profile emits the runtime evidence companion's records, including a Refusal Record, for every decision and pre-evaluation refusal; a PDP claiming only the Decision Base records decisions and refusals in its own internal form (#703, closing the unconditional-adoption-gate defect #703 identified)

requirements.text: A PDP conforming to this binding SHOULD advertise in its metadata `supported_obligations` array each obligation type it supports

observation.normative: a conforming PDP advertises each obligation type it supports in its metadata supported_obligations array

requirements.text: A compromised or misconfigured Access Request Service can auto-approve escalations, so it MUST be trusted, authenticated, and access-controlled like the PDP, and its auto-approval is bounded as above.

observation.normative: the Access Request Service is trusted, authenticated, and access-controlled to the same standard as the PDP

requirements.text: The PDP endpoint MUST be served over TLS 1.2 or later (TLS 1.3 RECOMMENDED). PEP-to-PDP authentication MUST be mutual, satisfying the integrity and mutual-authentication requirement the runtime profile places on the PEP-PDP channel

observation.normative: the PDP endpoint is served over TLS 1.2 or later, and PEP-to-PDP authentication is mutual

requirements.text: The PEP SHOULD minimize the denial detail it relays to the agent; a generic refusal suffices to stop the action, and the full reason and contributing constraints belong in evidence, not in the agent-facing response.

observation.normative: the PEP relays a minimized, generic denial to the agent-facing surface, keeping the full denial reason and contributing constraints in evidence rather than the agent response, and a deployment rate-limits access requests per Mission to bound denial-oracle probing

requirements.text: A PDP conforming to the Decision Base MUST advertise the full URN `urn:ietf:params:authzen:mission-runtime`, never the bare capability name.

observation.normative: a conforming PDP's metadata capabilities array advertises the full urn:ietf:params:authzen:mission-runtime URN for the Decision Base, never the bare capability name

requirements.notes: The base AuthZEN Authorization API 1.0 is pinned in notes/external-pins.json (id AUTHZEN, openid/authzen commit 2b07366d2dfd7ad9e2dedf44b97bd41e8a2b8c63, status established at Ship 3), so this row's upstream registry surface is verifiable against that snapshot.

requirements.text: A PDP that additionally conforms to a feature profile MUST advertise that profile's own capability URN as well; a PDP MUST NOT advertise a feature-profile URN it does not conform to.

observation.normative: a PDP's advertised capabilities array carries a feature-profile URN if and only if the PDP actually conforms to that feature profile

requirements.text: A PEP MUST NOT rely on a feature profile whose URN the PDP's advertised `capabilities` does not include: an unadvertised profile fails closed exactly as an absent one does elsewhere in this document ({{profiles-and-capabilities}}).

observation.normative: a PEP treats a feature profile absent from the PDP's advertised capabilities the same as a profile the deployment never composed: it fails closed rather than assuming the profile's behavior

requirements.text: Capability advertisement is PDP-declared, never requester-selected: nothing in a PEP's request selects, enables, or negotiates a feature profile, and a requester cannot omit a required profile to downgrade enforcement ({{profiles-and-capabilities}}).

observation.normative: no PEP request member selects, enables, or negotiates a feature profile; profile composition is fixed by deployment/PDP configuration, not by anything the requester supplies on a given request

requirements.text: A binding MUST define a Mission Reference that is:

observation.normative: the Mission Reference is stable for the lifetime and retention period of the Mission Context, unambiguous within the declared Controller namespace, and never reassigned to a different Mission Context within that namespace

requirements.text: If the native reference is not globally unambiguous, the binding MUST define the Controller identifier or other namespace value with which it is compared.

observation.normative: when the reference alone is not globally unambiguous, the binding names the namespace value compared alongside it

requirements.text: A reference disclosed beyond the Controller MUST NOT be guessable by parties outside the Mission's authorized set

observation.normative: a disclosed reference resists guessing by unauthorized parties: satisfied by at least 128 bits of reference entropy, a reference derived from undisclosed content, or a namespace whose every keyed surface authenticates the caller and does not disclose existence

tests.name: mission reference unguessability (@spec mission-substrate#reference) > the Mission Reference's random component carries at least 128 bits of entropy
mission reference unguessability (@spec mission-substrate#reference) > newMissionId draws at least 18 bytes (144 bits) from a caller-injected random source
mission reference unguessability (@spec mission-substrate#reference) > newMissionId's default source is node:crypto's randomBytes and needs no argument
mission reference unguessability (@spec mission-substrate#reference) > successive draws are distinct (sanity check, not a substitute for the entropy proof above)
mission reference unguessability (@spec mission-substrate#reference) > the four known msn_ minting sites all call the single newMissionId helper
mission reference unguessability (@spec mission-substrate#reference) > no file in kernel/ other than mission-id.ts itself constructs an msn_ id inline

requirements.notes: Length alone is not entropy, so Mission ID generation is now centralized into one helper (src/services/authorization-server/src/kernel/mission-id.ts's newMissionId), built on node:crypto's randomBytes, and all four msn_ minting sites (kernel.ts insertRecord, expansion.ts, child-delegation.ts, template.ts) were updated to call it instead of constructing the id inline. The helper itself is tested directly: one test injects an observing wrapper around the source function and asserts the helper requests exactly MISSION_ID_ENTROPY_BYTES (18, 144 bits, above the 128-bit floor this row's normative text names as one of three satisfying conditions), proving the entropy claim is about the source and byte count, not merely the length of one identifier from one call site; a second test exercises the default parameter (node:crypto's randomBytes with no argument supplied), decodes the exact byte count, AND reads mission-id.ts's own source to confirm the default is bound to the imported node:crypto randomBytes, not a same-named local; a distinctness sanity check over 1000 draws is additional, not a substitute for the entropy proof. The last two tests close the site-coverage class, not just four known instances: one confirms each known site calls newMissionId(), the other scans every file in kernel/ (not a fixed list) and asserts none but mission-id.ts itself still constructs `msn_${...}` inline, so a fifth minting site added later in a new file would still be caught. No negative-class row exists anywhere in the manifest for the mission-reference surface, so that half of the per-surface minimum is not expressible from this manifest as authored.

requirements.text: The binding MUST define how a relying component identifies the Controller responsible for the reference.

observation.normative: a relying component has a defined mechanism (local configuration, protocol identifier, trust anchor, or other substrate-native mechanism) for identifying the accountable Controller

This is the client-Actor binding, distinct from the existing approval_basis tests (mission#approval-basis), which cover the consenting human (Approver), a different substrate role.

requirements.text: The value MUST be derived from authenticated context or verified proof; it MUST NOT be accepted solely from an unauthenticated proposal.

observation.normative: the Actor handle comes from authenticated context or verified proof; an unauthenticated proposal alone never establishes it

requirements.text: The binding MUST state:

observation.normative: the binding states what the Actor handle identifies, how the Controller establishes it at approval, and how a later positive governance decision establishes that the acting party is the bound Actor or an authorized delegate

requirements.text: A binding that maps between identifiers MUST define which component performs the mapping and the assurance and ambiguity of that mapping.

observation.normative: a binding that maps between identifier syntaxes names the mapping component and states the mapping's assurance and ambiguity

requirements.text: The binding MUST maintain either the Approved Context itself or a verifiable commitment to it.

observation.normative: the binding maintains either the Approved Context or a verifiable commitment to it

tests.name: approved context commitment (@spec mission-substrate#approved-context) > all three Approved Context components (intent, proposal, derived authority_set) and their anchors survive successive state transitions unchanged

requirements.notes: The Approved Context is the Mission Intent, the recorded authority proposal where one was submitted, and the derived Authority Set ({{oauth-mission#oauth-statement}} item 4), not the Authority Set alone. The kernel's missions table (kernel.ts insertRecord) persists all three components (intent_json, proposed_authority_json, authority_set_json) and all three typed anchors (intent_hash, proposal_hash, authority_hash) together at creation; no UPDATE statement anywhere in kernel.ts ever touches any of those six columns (grep-verified: the only UPDATEs touch state/version/successor/grant_id/status_list_idx/containment_json/derivation_count/projected_from). The cited test approves a Mission WITH a submitted proposal (so all three components and all three anchors are actually present, not template-mode nulls), snapshots each by content, and re-verifies all six byte-for-byte across two successive transitions (suspend then resume) while state and version visibly advance.

requirements.text: After approval, the approved value MUST be immutable.

observation.normative: the approved value never changes after approval

tests.name: approved context commitment (@spec mission-substrate#approved-context) > all three Approved Context components (intent, proposal, derived authority_set) and their anchors survive successive state transitions unchanged

requirements.notes: Same kernel.ts persistence as maintain-or-commit above, for all three components: intent_json, proposed_authority_json, and authority_set_json (and their three anchors) are written once at insertRecord and never appear in any subsequent UPDATE statement; setState only ever writes state/version (and, for contain(), a separate containment_json overlay). The cited test transitions a Mission approved with a submitted proposal through two successive transitions and asserts all three components and all three anchors are unchanged by content (a snapshot comparison), not merely by reference.

requirements.text: Mutable operational fields, including current state and log entries, MUST be distinguishable from the approved value.

observation.normative: mutable operational fields (current state, log entries) are distinguishable from the immutable approved value

requirements.text: A binding MUST NOT silently replace the approved value behind an existing reference.

observation.normative: the approved value behind an existing reference is never silently replaced

requirements.text: Changing the Approved Context requires a new approval event and a new Mission Reference, unless a binding defines the change as approval of a new immutable version with its own unambiguous reference.

observation.normative: a changed Approved Context gets a new approval event and new Mission Reference, or an explicitly defined new immutable version with its own unambiguous reference

requirements.text: When a binding uses a commitment instead of retaining or disclosing the value, it MUST define:

observation.normative: the binding defines the exact committed bytes or canonicalization procedure, algorithm identification and agility behavior, domain separation sufficient to prevent cross-type substitution, and how a possessing party verifies the commitment

requirements.text: Every committed JSON value, and the envelope around it, MUST satisfy I-JSON

observation.normative: committed JSON values and their envelope satisfy I-JSON; non-conformant input destined for commitment is rejected before canonicalization: duplicate member names are refused at parse time before the parsed data model exists, string data is valid Unicode free of surrogate/noncharacter code points, and number data is representable as a finite IEEE 754 binary64 value

tests.name: parseStrictJson > rejects duplicate member names (core § canonicalization)

The I-JSON string (surrogate/noncharacter) and number (finite binary64) conformance arms have no test.

requirements.text: A verifier MUST reject a digest whose algorithm prefix it does not recognize and MUST NOT treat an unrecognized prefix as `sha-256`.

observation.normative: an unrecognized algorithm prefix is rejected outright and never silently compared as sha-256

requirements.text: a specification introducing a new prefix MUST define the carrier and schema of any parallel commitment, the binding that proves the old and new values commit to the same object, producer behavior during the transition, verifier selection and downgrade behavior when recognition sets differ, and the transition procedure itself.

observation.normative: a specification introducing a new digest-prefix algorithm defines the carrier and schema of any parallel commitment, the binding that proves the old and new values commit to the same object, producer behavior during the transition, verifier selection and downgrade behavior when recognition sets differ, and the transition procedure itself; no transition mechanism exists in this document, so an introducing specification carries the whole duty

requirements.text: A binding MUST define a native approval ceremony that atomically creates an active Mission Context or has equivalent transactional semantics.

observation.normative: the approval ceremony creates the active Mission Context atomically, or with equivalent transactional semantics: a failed creation leaves no partial record

tests.name: store baseline (D27) > transactions are atomic

This is a generic-infrastructure match rather than a @spec-tagged substrate test, recorded here for honesty.

requirements.text: The ceremony MUST:
