requirements.text: A binding MUST identify security-relevant material supplied by an untrusted proposer and describe how the approval ceremony prevents it from being mistaken for Controller-derived policy or trusted explanation.

observation.normative: the binding identifies untrusted-proposer-supplied security-relevant material and describes how the ceremony prevents it from being mistaken for Controller-derived policy or trusted explanation

requirements.text: Every binding MUST define an active predicate and a non-active outcome.

observation.normative: the binding defines an active predicate and a non-active outcome over its state vocabulary

tests.name: basic governance gate: state-gated issuance and derivation (@spec mission-substrate#basic-gate) > active predicate true -> gateActive and gateDerivation proceed
basic governance gate: state-gated issuance and derivation (@spec mission-substrate#basic-gate) > active predicate false -> gateActive and gateDerivation refuse, for every recognized non-active state

requirements.notes: The Controller is the Mission Issuer/AS ({{oauth-mission#oauth-statement}} item 2), not the resource-side PDP: the Basic Governance Gate is realized by src/services/authorization-server/src/kernel/kernel.ts's gateActiveLineage, shared by gateActive (state-gated issuance/continuation) and gateDerivation (state-gated derivation, layering the max_derivations cap on top). The active predicate is `record.state === "active"` exactly; the non-active outcome is a thrown GateError, refusing both issuance and derivation. Both cited tests run unconditionally against the kernel's in-memory sqlite store, so this coverage never sandbox-skips. The PDP's evaluate.ts implements the analogous RESOURCE-side decision gate (a different Controller-vs-PDP role per the substrate's binding statement); its four basic-gate-shaped unit tests now back the runtime/authzen decision-request rows they genuinely prove (see runtime.decision-inputs.active-state-required and runtime.decision-inputs.authority-entry-and-subset-required and authzen.pdp-request.consistency-id-and-issuer-equal), not this Controller-role row.

requirements.text: The Controller MUST make a positive governance decision only while the Mission is active.

observation.normative: a positive governance decision is made only while the Mission is active

tests.name: basic governance gate: state-gated issuance and derivation (@spec mission-substrate#basic-gate) > active predicate false -> gateActive and gateDerivation refuse, for every recognized non-active state

requirements.notes: Same gateActiveLineage predicate as active-predicate-and-outcome above, on the Controller (AS kernel), not the resource-side PDP. The cited test sweeps every recognized non-active MissionState (suspended, revoked, expired, completed, superseded, cascaded), persisting each directly on the record before asserting both gateActive and gateDerivation throw GateError, never a positive decision.

requirements.text: Every value or condition not recognized as active MUST fail closed for that decision.

observation.normative: any value or condition not recognized as active fails the decision closed

tests.name: basic governance gate: state-gated issuance and derivation (@spec mission-substrate#basic-gate) > a persisted state value outside the recognized lifecycle set fails closed, never treated as active

requirements.notes: This row's 'unrecognized' is a lifecycle value or condition, not an unknown action; an unmapped action is out_of_authority on the resource-side PDP, a different failure mode on a different actor (see runtime.decision-inputs.authority-entry-and-subset-required, which the PDP's unmapped-action test now backs instead). The cited kernel test writes a state string outside the MissionState set directly onto the persisted record (bypassing the type system, simulating a corrupted or future-versioned value) and asserts both gateActive and gateDerivation throw GateError with reason mission_not_active: the active predicate is a whitelist (state === "active"), so any unrecognized value fails closed by construction, never by an explicit blocklist entry that could omit a case.

requirements.text: The binding MUST define at least one authenticated means by which an authorized party can cause the Mission to become non-active.

observation.normative: the binding names an authenticated non-active-transition mechanism, identifies the authorized parties, and states the effect on subsequent Controller decisions

requirements.text: Authority derived from a Mission MUST NOT be usable indefinitely.

observation.normative: for every positive decision and every governed artifact, the binding states a reliance bound as either a maximum post-non-active residual interval or an artifact expiry bounded by/disclosed with the Approved Context; a decision or artifact with neither bound does not conform

tests.name: async-delegation terminal paths (@spec async-delegation) > absolute-lifetime clamp: the initial access token exp never exceeds the Mission expires_at

requirements.notes: core.tokens.exp-clamp tests the artifact-expiry-bound arm for core's issued credentials (exp capped by the Mission's expires_at). The decision-point residual-interval arm, and the general non-conformance-without-either-bound check, are untested at this generic level.

requirements.text: a stated bound SHOULD NOT exceed the interval the Mission's purpose requires

observation.normative: the stated reliance bound is no longer than the Mission's purpose requires

requirements.text: Each positive governance decision and each artifact that a binding claims is Mission-governed MUST carry, or be unambiguously joinable to, the Mission Reference and Controller namespace.

observation.normative: every governed decision or artifact carries, or is unambiguously joinable to, the Mission Reference and Controller namespace, and the binding defines the join and the party performing it

tests.name: M4 core enforcement tier > scenario 2: happy path -- in-authority read permitted, Decision Evidence recorded
M4 core enforcement tier > Decision Evidence carries the PDP emitter and the recomputable entry_digest

requirements.notes: Partial: the M4 enforcement tests thread the Mission Reference (mission_id) from the PDP request through the PEP decision to the retained Decision Evidence record, attributed to its emitter; a genuine cross-component chain (PDP, PEP, EvidenceStore). The underlying tests are tagged endpoint-level under their existing rows (runtime.evidence.decision-and-refusal-must-produce-record and others), so this row's cross-component level is not matched and it stays partial rather than tested. The Controller-namespace half is implicit (a single-issuer deployment), not a separately carried field, and this mapping does not exercise it.

requirements.text: Merely accepting an unverified reference supplied by the Actor does not establish Mission governance.

observation.normative: an unverified Actor-supplied reference, accepted without more, does not establish Mission governance

tests.name: basic gate: active predicate, non-active outcome, unrecognized-fails-closed > a supplied mission reference that mismatches the loaded view is refused, never silently accepted

requirements.notes: Partial: the cited unit-level test (unconditional, no live OpenFGA) proves a supplied context.mission.authority_hash that mismatches the independently loaded view is refused (view_inconsistent), never silently accepted. It does not prove the complementary half of this row's normative text, that an accepted reference must itself have arrived inside a verified credential rather than as a bare unauthenticated parameter; that is a token-binding/RS concern outside evaluate()'s pure-function boundary and untested here.

requirements.text: The binding MUST state what the propagation mechanism proves.  In particular, it MUST distinguish among:

observation.normative: the binding distinguishes correlation with a Mission Context, proof the Controller made a particular decision, proof a credential was issued under the Mission, and proof a requested operation is within approved structured authority; the kernel requires only the first, with authenticated or integrity-protected provenance

requirements.text: The Controller MUST maintain an integrity-protected, ordered record of governance events for the Mission.

observation.normative: the Controller maintains an integrity-protected, ordered governance-event record for the Mission

requirements.notes: The Controller MUST maintain this record ({{oauth-mission#oauth-statement}} item 9: the governance record is the Mission Record with its approval evidence and lifecycle history), not the resource-side PEP. mcp-payments's EvidenceStore (src/services/mcp-payments/src/evidence.ts) is a PEP-side, in-memory, unsigned array of per-request decision/refusal evidence; it satisfies no arm of a Controller-maintained record and its test does not establish Controller-role coverage, so it is not cited here. No Controller-owned governance record exists in src/ yet: the Mission Kernel's approval and lifecycle-transition events (kernel.ts approve()/setState()) fan out only through the ephemeral onLifecycleCommit callback and are never journaled into any persisted, queryable, integrity-protected record. The mcp-payments evidence tests remain cited, correctly, on the runtime-evidence rows they do prove (see evidence.refusal.per-attempt-immutable-append-only and the M4 enforcement-tier rows).

requirements.text: At minimum, the record MUST cover approval, positive and negative Controller decisions that rely on the Mission Context, and transition to a non-active outcome.

observation.normative: the record covers approval, positive and negative reliance decisions, and the non-active transition; events are attributable to their source and correlated with the Mission Reference

requirements.notes: The Controller MUST maintain this record ({{oauth-mission#oauth-statement}} item 9), not the resource-side PEP; mcp-payments's EvidenceStore records are PEP-side per-request decision evidence, not the Mission Record's approval evidence and lifecycle history, so they satisfy no arm of this row's minimum coverage (approval, positive/negative Controller decisions, and the non-active transition) and are not cited here. No Controller-owned record exists in src/ today: Mission Kernel approval and lifecycle-transition events (kernel.ts approve()/setState()) fan out only through the ephemeral onLifecycleCommit callback, never journaled into any persisted, queryable record. The mcp-payments decision-evidence tests remain cited, correctly, on the runtime-evidence Decision Evidence rows they do prove (the M4 enforcement-tier rows).

requirements.text: The binding MUST state its ordering semantics, integrity protection, authorized readers, and retention period.

observation.normative: the binding states the record's ordering semantics, integrity protection, authorized readers, and retention period

requirements.text: The retention period MUST include the active lifetime and a declared post-termination period.

observation.normative: the stated retention period spans the active lifetime plus a declared post-termination period

requirements.text: A binding MUST NOT claim a capability unless it meets every requirement in that capability's subsection.

observation.normative: a capability is claimed only when every requirement in its subsection is met

requirements.text: such scope is part of the claim and MUST appear in the Mission Substrate Statement

observation.normative: a capability's mode/role/operation/deployment scope is documented in the Mission Substrate Statement, not left implicit

requirements.text: Its Statement MUST enumerate those operations, such as authority derivation, delegation, credential issuance, credential refresh, permission decisions, or continued reliance.

observation.normative: the Statement enumerates the named authorization operations the Lifecycle-Gated Authorization claim covers

requirements.text: For every operation in the claim, the decision point MUST establish that the Mission is currently active before returning a positive result.

observation.normative: the decision point confirms current active state before returning a positive result, for every claimed operation

requirements.text: It MUST fail closed when current state cannot be established within the binding's stated freshness bound.

observation.normative: the decision point fails closed when current state cannot be established within the stated freshness bound

requirements.text: The binding MUST state the maximum interval during which a previously issued positive result can remain usable after the Mission becomes non-active.

observation.normative: the binding states the maximum post-non-active residual usability interval for a previously issued positive result

requirements.text: It MUST NOT generalize the narrower claim to the uncovered path.

observation.normative: a Lifecycle-Gated Authorization claim scoped to one operation class is never presented as covering an uncovered path

requirements.text: A binding claiming **State-Observable** MUST expose at least one authenticated, integrity-protected source from which a named consumer can determine whether a Mission is active.

observation.normative: at least one authenticated, integrity-protected source exposes whether a Mission is active to a named consumer

tests.name: caller authentication (@spec mission#caller-authorization-and-minimization) > refuses an unauthenticated call with 401 + WWW-Authenticate

requirements.notes: core's introspection endpoint is the concrete instantiation core's Mission Substrate Statement names for this capability; core.introspection.caller-authentication tests the authenticated-source property for that instantiation. Generic integrity-protection and the multi-source case beyond introspection are untested at this level.

requirements.text: For each source, the Statement MUST identify:

observation.normative: the Statement identifies the authorized consumers, the state vocabulary and active predicate, authentication and integrity protection, the freshness or maximum staleness bound, and fail-closed behavior for unavailable, invalid, or unknown state

requirements.text: A projection onto another protocol's vocabulary MUST preserve the active/non-active distinction; an unknown or non-active native value MUST NOT project to active.

observation.normative: a projection onto another protocol's vocabulary never maps an unknown or non-active native value to active

tests.name: composite non-active: active:false WITH mission.state (@spec mission#composite-active) > revoked Mission + valid token: only { active, mission }, state revoked, NO top-level or mission authorization_details
composite non-active: active:false WITH mission.state (@spec mission#composite-active) > Mission-expired composite: active:false with state expired

requirements.notes: core.introspection.composite-active exercises this exact projection rule (revoked/expired never project to active) for core's own instantiation.

requirements.text: A binding claiming **Structured Authority** MUST define a machine-evaluable representation of authority associated with the Mission and MUST identify the authority that owns the representation's semantics.

observation.normative: the binding defines a machine-evaluable authority representation and identifies the authority that owns its semantics

requirements.text: The Statement MUST specify:

observation.normative: the Statement specifies the representation and its version/type rules, how resources/operations/constraints are interpreted, which decision points consume it, whether it is approved context/Controller-derived policy/resource-owned input/decision result, and the scope in which two values compare

requirements.text: Where constraints admit comparison, the binding MUST define comparison in the constraint's value space.  Unknown types or constraints MUST fail closed at a decision point that requires their semantics.

observation.normative: comparison is defined in the constraint's value space, and unknown types or constraints fail closed at any decision point requiring their semantics

requirements.text: A binding claiming **Monotonic Derivation** MUST also claim Structured Authority for the values covered by the derivation.

observation.normative: a Monotonic Derivation claim always pairs with a Structured Authority claim for the covered values

requirements.text: It MUST define a no-broader-than relation for those values and the protocol boundary within which that relation is valid.

observation.normative: the binding defines a no-broader-than relation for the covered values and the protocol boundary within which it is valid

requirements.text: Every derivation, delegation, or attenuation operation included in the claim MUST verify that its result is no broader than its declared parent under that relation.  Unsupported or incomparable values MUST fail closed.

observation.normative: every covered derivation/delegation/attenuation verifies its result is no broader than its declared parent; unsupported or incomparable values fail closed

tests.name: toolsSubset (capability monotonicity) > adding a tool the parent lacks is NOT a subset (widen)
verifyAttenuationChain > WIDEN by raising the cap on the child is refused (capability_widened)

requirements.notes: core's attenuation-chain verifier (packages/mission-core) tests the no-broader-than narrowing check extensively (widen refused on tools, ranges, aud, exp, and delegation depth) for core's own claim. The unsupported-or-incomparable-values-fail-closed arm is untested at this generic level.

requirements.text: Every covered transition is classified as exactly one of:

observation.normative: each covered transition is classified as exactly one of preserve, attenuate, or decide_anew; incomparability routes to refusal or decide_anew, and a translation between vocabularies is never silently treated as attenuation

requirements.text: It MUST NOT be presented as constraining fresh authorization decisions made under a different resource-owned policy or at an uncovered protocol hop.

observation.normative: a Monotonic Derivation claim is never presented as constraining a fresh decision under a different resource-owned policy or at an uncovered hop

requirements.text: A binding claiming **Credential-Bound** MUST define an integrity-protected association between a credential or authorization artifact and exactly one Mission Reference and Controller namespace.

observation.normative: the binding defines an integrity-protected association between a credential/artifact and exactly one Mission Reference and Controller namespace

requirements.text: It MUST identify:

observation.normative: the binding identifies the protected fields or join inputs establishing the association, the credential/artifact issuer and verifier trust relationship, how the credential is bound to the Actor or authorized delegate, substitution and replay protections, and whether issuance or refresh is covered by Lifecycle-Gated Authorization

requirements.text: A reference copied from Actor-controlled input without Controller or credential-issuer validation does not satisfy this capability.

observation.normative: a reference copied from Actor-controlled input, without Controller or credential-issuer validation, does not satisfy Credential-Bound

requirements.text: A Credential-Bound claim MUST select which of the following fact semantics the mechanism establishes, and a claim MUST NOT say "Mission-bound" without that selection:

observation.normative: the claim selects among correlation only, artifact issuance under the Mission, authority derivation under the Mission, lifecycle-gated issuance, or current state as of an observation; a bare "Mission-bound" label without that selection does not satisfy the capability

requirements.text: the issued-under and correlation-only semantics MUST NOT share an unqualified claim

observation.normative: the issued-under-the-Mission semantics and the correlation-only semantics never ride under one unqualified claim

requirements.text: A binding claiming **Authorized Context Correlation** MUST supply an authorized association among independently established facts, such as the Mission, the Subject, the Actor (and the Deployment and executing instance where the binding distinguishes them), an authority artifact, a request or transaction, and a target resource.

observation.normative: the binding supplies an authorized association among the independently established facts it names (Mission, Subject, Actor, authority artifact, request/transaction, target resource, and any distinguished Deployment/executing instance)

requirements.text: The claim MUST identify the joining authority, the association policy, the proof inputs, conflict handling, the association's lifetime and revocation, its audience, and its substitution protection.

observation.normative: the claim identifies the joining authority, association policy, proof inputs, conflict handling, lifetime/revocation, audience, and substitution protection

requirements.text: Matching strings or timestamps do not satisfy this capability: the association is an authorized fact established by the joining authority, not an observation that two values coincide.

observation.normative: coincidence of strings or timestamps never satisfies the capability; only an authorized fact established by the joining authority does

requirements.text: A binding claiming **Independently Verifiable** MUST let the named consumer verify a specified Mission property without an online query to the Controller.

observation.normative: the named consumer verifies the specified property without an online query to the Controller

requirements.text: The Statement MUST enumerate the properties, for example Controller approval, context commitment, credential binding, structured authority, or state as of a signed observation.

observation.normative: the Statement enumerates each independently verifiable property the claim covers

requirements.text: For every property, the binding MUST define the verification artifact, canonical input, trust anchor or key discovery mechanism, algorithm agility, validity interval, and revocation or freshness limitations.

observation.normative: for every enumerated property, the binding defines the verification artifact, canonical input, trust anchor/key discovery, algorithm agility, validity interval, and revocation/freshness limitations

requirements.text: Verification failure or an unsupported algorithm MUST fail closed.

observation.normative: a verification failure or unsupported algorithm fails closed

requirements.text: A binding claiming **Portable Evidence** MUST define evidence that can be transferred across the administrative boundary stated in the claim and verified there.

observation.normative: the binding defines evidence transferable across the claim's stated administrative boundary and verifiable there

requirements.text: The Statement MUST identify:

observation.normative: the Statement identifies each evidence type and the event/decision it represents, its binding to the Mission Reference/Controller/Actor/relevant decision or artifact, canonical bytes/integrity protection/verification procedure, ordering/duplicate-handling/correlation semantics, retention and key-availability periods, and disclosure/minimization/unlinkability considerations

requirements.text: defines fail-closed behavior when a required reference, binding, state, authority value, commitment, proof, or capability cannot be established

observation.normative: a conforming binding fails closed whenever a required reference, binding, state, authority value, commitment, proof, or capability cannot be established, generalizing the basic-gate and capability-confusion fail-closed rules to every kernel and capability element

requirements.text: A specification that itself claims conformance to this document MUST contain a section titled "Mission Substrate Statement"

observation.normative: a conforming binding publishes a section titled "Mission Substrate Statement" identifying the specification version and mode it applies to

requirements.text: For the kernel, the Statement MUST provide a checkable mapping for:

observation.normative: the Statement provides a checkable mapping for all nine kernel items: the Mission Reference's uniqueness/comparison/retention/non-reassignment/unguessability treatment; Controller identity establishment; the Actor handle's authentication/binding/delegation/identifier mappings; the Approved Context's immutable boundary and commitment/verification; each approval-ceremony step; the active predicate, non-active outcome, transition mechanisms, and decision effect; the bounded-reliance bound per decision/artifact class; every propagation/join surface and the property it proves; and governance-record coverage, ordering, integrity, access, and retention

requirements.text: The Statement MUST then include a capability table with one row for each capability in {{capabilities}}.

observation.normative: the Statement includes a capability table with one row for each of the eight optional capabilities

requirements.text: Each row MUST say `supplied` or `not supplied`

observation.normative: a capability row states supplied or not supplied; there is no third (retired conditional) state

requirements.text: A supplied row MUST:

observation.normative: a supplied row cites the satisfying binding sections, states its mode and operational scope, states its activation conditions (or `always`), states its temporal elements (freshness at use, decision/artifact lifetime, and post-non-active residual interval, each stated directly or expressly inherited from the bounded-reliance floor), states its failure behavior for absent/stale/unknown/incomparable/invalid/unavailable input, and lists material limitations

requirements.text: Text outside the Statement cannot silently broaden a capability claim.

observation.normative: no text outside the published Statement broadens a capability claim

requirements.text: If another specification adds a capability, that specification MUST publish an updated Statement or a Statement extension that identifies the base binding and precise added scope.

observation.normative: a specification adding a capability publishes an updated Statement, or a Statement extension naming the base binding and the precise added scope

requirements.text: A substrate-neutral profile MUST declare the kernel functions and optional capabilities it consumes.

observation.normative: a substrate-neutral profile declares, in its own text, the kernel functions and the optional capabilities it consumes

requirements.text: It MUST NOT infer an undeclared capability from the generic statement that a binding supports Missions.

observation.normative: a substrate-neutral profile never infers an undeclared capability merely from a binding's generic claim to support Missions; only a capability actually declared, per the previous requirement, is consumed

requirements.text: The adapter's specification MUST state the new trust assumptions, what it proves, what it cannot prove, and its failure behavior.

observation.normative: where a profile defines an explicit adapter or join to supply a capability a binding lacks, the adapter's own specification states the new trust assumptions it introduces, what it proves, what it cannot prove, and its failure behavior

requirements.text: Specifications MUST preserve those boundaries rather than describe the whole deployment with the stronger local property.

observation.normative: a specification describing a capability that composes only over a declared scope never describes the whole deployment as carrying the stronger local property that scope does not reach

requirements.text: A secure implementation fails closed when a required capability is absent, claimed with unmet activation conditions, or outside its declared scope.

observation.normative: an absent capability, one claimed with unmet activation conditions, or one used outside its declared scope, fails the relying decision closed

requirements.text: It does not upgrade a kernel-only reference because its syntax resembles a credential claim or content digest.

observation.normative: a kernel-only reference is never upgraded to a stronger capability's guarantee merely because its syntax resembles a credential claim or content digest

requirements.text: a consumer MUST NOT treat co-presentation of independently valid facts as an authorized association

observation.normative: a consumer never treats the mere co-presentation of independently valid identity evidence, credential, and Mission as an authorized association; Authorized Context Correlation is required whenever one authority did not itself bind all the required facts

requirements.text: The Statement MUST identify each narrowing point and the component that performs the comparison.

observation.normative: the Statement identifies every narrowing point in the covered derivation/delegation/attenuation flow and the component performing each comparison

requirements.text: Bindings SHOULD disclose a reference only to components that require Mission correlation

observation.normative: a Mission Reference is disclosed only to components that require Mission correlation

requirements.text: SHOULD prefer audience-specific derived handles where cross-context correlation is unnecessary

observation.normative: an audience-specific derived handle is used in place of the shared Mission Reference where cross-context correlation is unnecessary

requirements.text: A binding SHOULD minimize context in credentials, state responses, and evidence

observation.normative: Approved Context content carried in credentials, state responses, and evidence is minimized rather than carried in full

requirements.text: MUST document the additional disclosure introduced by Structured Authority, Independently Verifiable, or Portable Evidence claims

observation.normative: the additional disclosure introduced by a Structured Authority, Independently Verifiable, or Portable Evidence claim is documented

requirements.text: REQUIRED. A string. Unique record identifier for this Decision Evidence Object. ABNF: `1*64( ALPHA / DIGIT / "-" / "_" )`. At least 128 bits of entropy.

observation.normative: evidence_id conforms to the ABNF and carries at least 128 bits of entropy

requirements.text: REQUIRED. An object. The decision request's Mission reference object, extended with the facts below, so the evidence chains back to the exact approved Mission. Sub-members:

observation.normative: the record's mission object always carries the request's id/issuer/authority_hash (REQUIRED) and the PDP's own policy_view_id (REQUIRED, always populated whatever the request carried); intent_hash, policy_version, and a consent-disclosure commitment are OPTIONAL and recorded only when known; these hashes are the issuing AS's own commitments cited as anchors, never recomputed by the PDP

requirements.text: It MUST NOT contain the request's `properties.parameters`, under any name: the parameter binding this record carries is `parameter_digest` alone, an evidence projection of the decision request rather than a pass-through of it.

observation.normative: the action member never carries raw request parameters under any name; only parameter_digest carries the parameter binding

requirements.text: REQUIRED. A string. The runtime action class the PDP applied to the action: one of `consequential_read`, `consequential_write`, `irreversible_action`, `external_commitment`, or `privileged_administration`

observation.normative: action_class names one of the five runtime classes and is always present since every record here is on a consequential action; class_source (REQUIRED when action_class is present, i.e. always) records how the class was assigned: default, resource_floor, or deployment

requirements.text: This member MUST contain only claims the PEP verified before invoking the PDP.

observation.normative: the credential member never carries a claim the PEP did not itself verify before invoking the PDP

requirements.text: REQUIRED when `parameter_digest` is absent for a consequential action, so the closed object still carries the request digest the runtime profile requires of every decision record

observation.normative: parameter_digest is REQUIRED for a parameter-bound action; evaluation_request_digest is REQUIRED whenever parameter_digest is absent, so every decision record carries one digest or the other, present whether the decision was a permit or a deny

requirements.text: REQUIRED whenever the decision response contained obligations, on either decision. An array of obligation objects, recorded as returned to the PEP

observation.normative: obligations is present whenever the decision response carried obligations, on a permit or a deny alike, and records them exactly as returned to the PEP

requirements.text: the PDP MUST set `use_limit: 1` for a permit in the high-consequence classes

observation.normative: conditions is REQUIRED when decision is permit for a consequential action, recording valid_until and use_limit; the PDP sets use_limit to exactly 1 for a high-consequence-class permit, and the producer ensures the record's parameter_digest equals the parameter binding carried by the wire conditions

requirements.text: For a permit it records every constraint key and entry type the decision relied on; for a deny it MUST list every entry that failed. Omitting an entry the decision turned on is non-conforming.

observation.normative: contributing_constraints, required when the decision turned on one or more authority or constraint entries, lists every relied-on entry for a permit and every failing entry for a deny; omitting an entry the decision turned on is non-conforming

requirements.text: The sequence is scoped to the emitter identified by `emitter`: each emitter maintains its own monotonically increasing per-Mission sequence, and a verifier detects gaps and orders records within (Mission, emitter).

observation.normative: sequence is zero or greater and monotonically increasing per (Mission, emitter); cross-emitter ordering is best-effort from correlation members and timestamps, never reconstructed from sequence alone

tests.name: evaluate() emits the Decision Evidence it decided (@spec runtime-evidence#decision-evidence-object, #741) > allocates the emitter's OWN monotonic per-(Mission, emitter) sequence, which does not reset within a process
Decision Evidence per-(mission, emitter, role) sequence allocation > allocates a monotonically increasing sequence per role, independently per role, even under the SAME mission and emitter id

requirements.notes: Partial: the counter is the PDP emitter's own (#741), and monotonicity per (Mission, emitter) is asserted at the emission path and end to end through the real call sites. The row's cross-component level is not reached: gap detection and ordering across two independently running emitters have no second emitter in this deployment to order against, and the counter is in-memory per process, so it says nothing about ordering across a restart.

requirements.text: a consumer MUST treat an unrecognized value as a deny and MUST NOT attach any other semantics to it

observation.normative: a consumer treats an unrecognized denial_reason value as a deny and attaches no other semantics to it; a constraint-violation deny records `parameter_violation` in denial_reason with the specific failing keys in contributing_constraints, so the reason enum and the open constraint-key space never mix in one field

requirements.text: A record of a permit MUST carry `authorizing_entry` or `entry_digest`, per the runtime record requirements

observation.normative: every permit record carries authorizing_entry (the full entry) or entry_digest (its integrity-anchor encoded digest), the issuance profile's Authority Set entry commitment

requirements.text: Subject identifiers and assurance metadata, never a raw claim set, minimized per the deployment's audit policy.

observation.normative: the record's subject member carries subject identifiers and assurance metadata only, never a raw claim set, minimized per the deployment's audit policy

requirements.text: any further resource properties are minimized to what the deployment's audit policy declares

observation.normative: the record's resource member carries the resource identifier and type, and any further resource properties are minimized to what the deployment's audit policy declares

requirements.text: The runtime profile requires a decision evidence record for every PDP decision on a consequential action and fixes the minimum content and local integrity requirements.

observation.normative: the emitted Decision Evidence Object carries evidence_id (string), evaluation_id (string), mission (object), subject (object), resource (object), action (object), audience (string), action_class (string), decision (string, permit or deny), sequence (integer), emitter (object), evaluated_at (timestamp), and evidence_envelope (object) on every record; it also carries class_source (string) whenever action_class is present, obligations (array of objects) whenever the decision response carried obligations, conditions (object) whenever the decision is permit for a consequential action, and contributing_constraints (array of strings) whenever the decision turned on one or more constraint or authority entries

tests.name: evaluate() emits the Decision Evidence it decided (@spec runtime-evidence#decision-evidence-object, #741) > returns a signed record on a PERMIT that an independent verifier accepts
evaluate() emits the Decision Evidence it decided (@spec runtime-evidence#decision-evidence-object, #741) > returns a signed record on a DENY, carrying the PDP's own denial reason

requirements.notes: Partial. The emitted record carries the REQUIRED members and class_source, asserted against a decision the PDP actually reached rather than a hand-built object, and conditions ride a permit. Not witnessed: obligations (this deployment attaches none) and contributing_constraints (the PDP does not track which entries a decision turned on). capability_source is deliberately absent from the record (#741): the member left the decision request envelope with #657/#730, so no validated PDP-side input carries it, and a PEP-supplied copy would be caller-asserted record content. It returns once #657's per-action capability-binding resolver supplies it from the PDP's own verified inputs.

requirements.text: Actor-chain identifiers and assurance metadata, never a raw claim set, minimized per the deployment's audit policy.

observation.normative: when present, the record's actor member carries actor-chain identifiers and assurance metadata only, never a raw claim set, minimized per the deployment's audit policy

requirements.text: Credential-derived identifiers and assurance metadata, never a raw claim set, minimized per the deployment's audit policy.

observation.normative: when present, the record's credential member carries credential-derived identifiers and assurance metadata only, never a raw claim set, minimized per the deployment's audit policy

requirements.text: REQUIRED. A string. Unique refusal identifier. ABNF: `1*64( ALPHA / DIGIT / "-" / "_" )`. At least 128 bits of entropy.

observation.normative: refusal_id conforms to the ABNF and carries at least 128 bits of entropy

requirements.text: For a PEP refusal, one of `token_invalid`, `mission_claim_missing`, `mission_reference_conflict` (reference sources naming different Missions, or an unusable propagated reference where governance requires one, the Mission Reference Propagation channel's conflict rule, {{I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-authority-server}}), `channel_failure`, `pdp_unreachable`, or `state_unavailable`

observation.normative: denial_reason names a pre-evaluation condition (PEP-side: token_invalid, mission_claim_missing, channel_failure, pdp_unreachable, state_unavailable; PDP-side: mission_context_missing), disjoint from the runtime profile's evaluated-decision denial reasons; a record able to populate the PDP-derived members of an evaluated decision is a Decision Evidence Object instead, never a Refusal Record

requirements.text: REQUIRED when `parameter_digest` is absent, so the record meets the runtime profile's record minimum

observation.normative: parameter_digest is REQUIRED for a parameter-bound action class; evaluation_request_digest is REQUIRED whenever parameter_digest is absent, so a Refusal Record always carries one of the two digests

requirements.text: present only when the refusing component established it before the failure: for a PEP, for example, on `pdp_unreachable`; for a PDP refusing on `mission_context_missing`, the reference is typically absent, since that is exactly what the request lacked.

observation.normative: the Refusal Record's mission member is present only when the refusing component itself established the Mission reference before the failure occurred

requirements.text: For a token-validation failure, the record MUST NOT describe unverified token claims as authenticated facts

observation.normative: subject/actor/credential on a Refusal Record carry only verified facts; a PEP populates them from its own token validation and a PDP from the request context it received, and neither role attests a fact only the other could verify; on a token-validation failure, unverified claims are never described as authenticated

requirements.text: REQUIRED when the record carries a verified `mission` reference, continuing that emitter's per-Mission sequence for that Mission

observation.normative: sequence is REQUIRED exactly when the record carries a verified mission reference, continuing that emitter's ordinary per-Mission sequence; it is absent when no Mission was established

requirements.text: Refusal Records are per-attempt, immutable, and append-only: a sustained failure condition with a retrying agent yields one signed record per attempt, never a record amended or replaced in place.

observation.normative: each refusal attempt yields its own signed, immutable record; a retried failure never amends or replaces a prior record in place, and a derived summary over a series of records is not itself a Refusal Record and adds no evidentiary standing beyond its inputs

tests.name: Refusal Records are per-attempt, immutable, and append-only > a sustained parameter-mismatch condition yields one new record per attempt, never an amendment in place

requirements.notes: Tested: a sustained parameter_mismatch condition, retried twice, yields a second distinct record (append-only) whose content leaves the first record's own content unchanged (a snapshot comparison, not reference identity, so an in-place amendment would fail it). Not tested: 'signed' -- EvidenceStore retains plain objects; signing and SCITT registration are M10 future work per its own header comment.

requirements.text: absence of the `mission` claim is not a pre-decision refusal and `mission_claim_missing` does not apply; the external join's verification governs instead

observation.normative: when the deployment establishes the Mission binding externally under the runtime profile's binding-establishment step, a missing mission claim is not itself a pre-decision refusal condition

requirements.text: The runtime profile also requires an evidence record for a refusal that occurs before any PDP decision, whether the refusing component is the PEP or the PDP

observation.normative: the emitted Refusal Record carries refusal_id (string), audience (string), action (object), decision (string, always deny), denial_reason (string), evaluated_at (timestamp), emitter (object), and evidence_envelope (object) on every record

requirements.text: A verifier MUST perform the following steps, in order, and MUST NOT treat a record as verified if any step fails:

observation.normative: the four-step verification procedure (decode payload; recompute JCS canonical bytes with evidence_envelope removed; require byte equality; verify the JWS signature and header) runs in order, and a record is treated as verified only if every step succeeds

requirements.text: Require byte-for-byte equality between the decoded payload of step 1 and the canonical bytes of step 2, rejecting the record on any difference. The signature authenticates only its own embedded payload; an outer object that differs from that payload is unauthenticated, regardless of whether the signature itself verifies.

observation.normative: byte-for-byte equality between the decoded JWS payload and the recomputed canonical bytes of the outer record (envelope removed) is required; any difference rejects the record even if the embedded signature itself verifies, since the signature authenticates only its own payload

requirements.text: A verifier MUST confirm that the signing key selected by the JWS `kid` is the published key of the component named in the record's `emitter` member, and that this key is bound to the enforcement scope and audience the record serves

observation.normative: the verifier confirms the kid-selected key is the named emitter's published key and is bound to the enforcement scope and audience the record serves; a record whose signing key is not published for that scope is rejected, so one component's key cannot sign evidence for a resource, audience, or scope it does not serve

requirements.notes: Lines 487-489 (Decision Evidence's emitter member), 640-642 (Refusal Record's emitter member), and 1029-1031 (Execution Evidence's emitter member) each restate this rule with an explicit in-text cross-reference back to this anchor; treated as duplicate-of-another-row rather than three additional rows. The vacuity the prior note recorded is closed (#741): the emitter id and audience are the deployment's real values (its canonical resource and the request audience) rather than the ephemeral signer's placeholders, the binding is enforced on the emission side too (an emitter refuses to sign for a scope its key does not serve), and a record whose emitter id or audience does not resolve is refused at retention with nothing retained. observation.normative: when the selected signing key is identified as compromised, the compromise-boundary rule gates the signature-verification step itself: it applies before the signature can be treated as verified, not as a separate check after the fact

requirements.text: an implementation MAY offer other JOSE algorithms but MUST implement `ES256`

observation.normative: the protected header's kid resolves in the emitter's published JWKS, and ES256 is mandatory to implement (other JOSE algorithms may additionally be offered)

requirements.text: A verifier MUST reject a JWS whose protected `typ` is not `application/mission-runtime-evidence+jws` or whose protected `cty` is not the media type of the object it is verifying, so signatures over one record kind cannot be cross-used for another

observation.normative: the protected typ names the secured runtime-evidence representation and the protected cty names the record kind; a wrong value in either position is rejected, so cross-kind signature reuse is foreclosed

requirements.text: This document defines only the `jws-compact` format. Additional formats MAY be defined by future specifications; implementations MUST reject envelopes with unsupported formats.

observation.normative: an evidence_envelope whose format is not jws-compact, or another format a future specification defines and the implementation recognizes, is rejected rather than accepted unverified

requirements.notes: Line 1849 ("Implementations MUST reject evidence whose format is unsupported rather than accepting it unverified") restates this rule under evidence-integrity-signing-keys; treated as duplicate-of-another-row.

requirements.text: REQUIRED. A string. Unique execution identifier, stable across delivery retries of this record: exactly one Execution Evidence Object exists per final disposition of a permit, and delivery of that record is at-least-once

observation.normative: execution_id conforms to the ABNF, carries at least 128 bits of entropy, and stays stable across at-least-once delivery retries of the one Execution Evidence Object per final disposition

requirements.text: delivery of that record is at-least-once, so a consumer MUST deduplicate on `execution_id` rather than assume single delivery

observation.normative: a consumer deduplicates Execution Evidence deliveries on execution_id rather than assuming exactly-once delivery

requirements.text: Inequality is a parameter deviation, and the record REMAINS VALID: evidence of an unauthorized execution is still evidence, never grounds to discard the record.

observation.normative: when authorized_parameter_digest and effective_parameter_digest diverge, the record is a parameter deviation and remains a valid record, never discarded; a deviation recorded against outcome completed or failed is equally representable, and a consumer MUST flag it as an unauthorized execution

requirements.text: A deployment MAY define additional values, which MUST be collision-resistant names (a short name within a namespace the deployment controls, following the Collision-Resistant Name guidance of {{RFC7519}} Section 4.2) so they cannot collide with this set or another deployment's.

observation.normative: error is one of the closed set (parameter_mismatch, permit_expired, permit_consumed, obligation_unfulfilled, kill_switch) when outcome is failed or suppressed; a deployment-defined additional value must be a collision-resistant name

requirements.text: REQUIRED when the linked Decision Evidence carried obligations and a permit disposition exists. One object per attached obligation, with `id` (REQUIRED, a string, the obligation's identifier as returned by the decision), `type` (REQUIRED, a string, the obligation type), `outcome` (REQUIRED, a string, one of `fulfilled`, `failed`, or `unsupported`)

observation.normative: obligation_outcomes is REQUIRED whenever the linked Decision Evidence carried obligations and a permit disposition exists, with one object per attached obligation carrying id, type, and a fulfilled/failed/unsupported outcome

requirements.text: MUST NOT carry user-content payloads.

observation.normative: result_summary carries only minimal action result metadata (for example, affected resource counts), never user-content payloads

requirements.notes: Line 1938 ("The Execution Evidence result_summary MUST NOT carry user-content payloads") restates this in Privacy Considerations; treated as duplicate-of-another-row.

requirements.text: When the executing PEP detects the deviation before acting, it MUST refuse the action and emit Execution Evidence with `outcome` `suppressed` and `error` `parameter_mismatch`

observation.normative: an executing PEP that detects a parameter deviation before acting refuses the action and emits Execution Evidence with outcome suppressed and error parameter_mismatch, rather than proceeding; whatever the recorded outcome, an audit consumer MUST classify a detected digest divergence as a parameter deviation and treat it as equivalent to an unauthorized action for compliance purposes

requirements.text: Decision Evidence, Execution Evidence, and Refusal Records MUST be retained for at least the deployment's audit retention window, which the runtime profile requires to be no shorter than the Mission's audit horizon

observation.normative: all three record types are retained for at least the deployment's audit retention window, itself no shorter than the Mission's audit horizon; a regulated deployment may require longer retention

requirements.text: A verifier MUST verify the referenced records and the cross-record joins of {{receipt-verification}} before relying on any copied field

observation.normative: a verifier verifies the referenced records and cross-record joins before relying on any copied field, and additionally verifies the transparency commitment where transparency is claimed; a deployment may instead accept a copied field on the receipt signer's authority alone, but only under an explicit policy naming the receipt issuer as attesting that fact directly

requirements.text: It claims an authorization decision was rendered; it claims nothing about execution, and a verifier MUST NOT treat it as evidence that an action occurred.

observation.normative: a `decision`-kind receipt is never treated as evidence that an action occurred

requirements.text: an action whose outcome is not yet terminal has no `execution` receipt, and an unresolved action MUST NOT be rewritten as terminal to issue one

observation.normative: an execution-kind receipt is never issued by rewriting an unresolved action as terminal; it exists only once the linked Execution Evidence has a real terminal outcome

requirements.text: The member is this exact object, never a union with another projection.

observation.normative: the receipt's mission member is exactly {id, issuer, optionally authority_hash}, never unioned with fields from another projection

requirements.text: the statement declares which of them issue receipts; the verifier resolves the signing key through that statement's published key sets ({{evidence-integrity-signing-keys}}) and rejects an emitter the statement does not name as a receipt issuer. A self-published key presenting `role` `receipt_issuer` establishes nothing

observation.normative: receipt issuance is limited to components the deployment's enforcement scope statement names; a verifier rejects an emitter the statement does not name as a receipt issuer, and a self-published key presenting role receipt_issuer establishes nothing on its own

requirements.text: REQUIRED when `kind` is `execution`; absent otherwise. A string, copied from the projected Execution Evidence's `outcome`

observation.normative: outcome is REQUIRED exactly when kind is execution and absent otherwise, copied from the projected Execution Evidence's outcome unchanged

requirements.text: Everything beyond the join and integrity core is optional and selected, never defaulted: a projection profile or a recipient agreement names the optional members a receipt carries, and an issuer minimizes to that selection.

observation.normative: an issuer carries only the optional members a projection profile or recipient agreement selects, never every available member by default; a Mission Receipt is evidence, never reusable authorization, and confers no authority on its holder

requirements.text: REQUIRED when `issuer_assertions` is present.

observation.normative: the profile member (naming the projection profile in force) is REQUIRED whenever issuer_assertions is present

requirements.text: every member's name and semantics come from the `profile`, and relying on any of them takes the trust model's explicit-policy path, never the verified-projection path

observation.normative: issuer_assertions members are structurally separate from the projected members: their names and semantics come entirely from the named profile, and a relying party takes the explicit-policy trust path for them, never the verified-projection path the other members use

requirements.text: A Mission Receipt is the portable, tamper-evident projection of a Mission's runtime enforcement evidence: one signed object a holder can present to answer what was decided, and for an executed action what happened, without shipping a log.

observation.normative: the emitted Mission Receipt carries evidence_envelope (object), kind (string), mission (object), emitter (object), evidence (array), and issued_at (timestamp) on every receipt, and carries outcome (string) whenever kind is execution

requirements.text: A `sha-256:` prefixed digest, classified under the substrate's default commitment construction ({{I-D.draft-mcguinness-mission-substrate}}) as a canonical-object digest for a JSON evidence record and a raw-octet digest for a JWS- or JWT-shaped artifact.

observation.normative: an evidence reference's digest is a canonical-object digest (complete object, evidence_envelope included, JCS canonicalized) for a JSON evidence record, and a raw-octet digest over the exact serialization octets for a compact-serialized artifact

requirements.text: An `evidence` array carries the combination {{receipt-kinds}} fixes for the receipt's `kind`: one Decision Evidence reference alone for `decision`; a permit Decision Evidence reference and the final Execution Evidence reference of the same action for `execution`; one Refusal Record reference alone for `refusal`. A reference to a record type the verifier does not implement fails verification; it is not skipped.

observation.normative: the evidence array carries exactly the reference combination fixed for the receipt's kind (decision: one Decision Evidence; execution: a permit Decision Evidence plus the final Execution Evidence of the same action; refusal: one Refusal Record); a reference to an unimplemented record type fails verification rather than being silently skipped

requirements.text: Each `evidence` entry is an object. All members REQUIRED:

observation.normative: each evidence array entry carries type (string, the referenced record's registered media type), digest (string), evidence_id (string), and emitter (object), all REQUIRED

requirements.text: `previous` (an array of one or more digests of predecessor receipts in the same scope, present on every receipt after the stream's first)

observation.normative: chain carries stream (issuer-chosen identifier), sequence (strictly increasing per stream), and previous (one or more predecessor digests, present on every receipt after the stream's first); a predecessor digest is a canonical-object digest of the complete predecessor Mission Receipt object, evidence_envelope included, so it covers the signature and not only the unsigned payload; concurrent issuance either serializes per stream or records multiple predecessors, and a verifier treats the result as a DAG, checking linkage and sequence monotonicity, never completeness

requirements.text: A verifier MUST perform the following steps, in order, and MUST NOT rely on a receipt if any step fails.

observation.normative: the seven-step receipt verification procedure runs in order, and a receipt is relied on only if every step succeeds; the reject-on list (a missing required record, a record of an unimplemented type, digest mismatch, emitter or key mismatch, join failure, a chain-linkage failure, or a copied field that differs) enumerates what "any step fails" means

requirements.text: the receipt's Mission binding is established by the verified records and the joins of step 4, never by key publication alone

observation.normative: step 1 verifies the receipt's own evidence_envelope (byte equality, typ, and signature against the scope statement's published keys, confirming the statement names the emitter as a receipt issuer) but the receipt's Mission binding itself rests on the verified referenced records and their joins, never on key publication alone

requirements.text: Resolve each evidence reference. Verify each resolved record under its own rules ({{decision-evidence-integrity}}). Recompute each digest over the defined bytes ({{receipt-evidence}}) and require equality. Require the resolved record's own identifier to equal `evidence_id` and its emitter and key to match `emitter`.

observation.normative: step 3 resolves and independently verifies each referenced record, recomputes its digest and requires equality with the reference, and requires the resolved record's own identifier and emitter/key to match the reference

requirements.text: A RECEIPT ISSUER conforming to this document MUST:

requirements.text: a proof whose authenticated time is at or after the boundary does not

requirements.text:
A source that is unavailable, fails verification, or reports a state
`version` older than one already observed for this Mission is a
transient failure, never authority exhaustion, and is refused in a
machine-readable shape: this profile defines a token-endpoint use of
the OAuth `temporarily_unavailable` error code

observation.normative: an Effective Authority Set source that is unavailable, unverifiable, or reports a rolled-back state version is refused with the OAuth temporarily_unavailable error code and HTTP status 503 (machine-readable, not an error_description to parse), optionally carrying Retry-After, and is never treated as authority exhaustion nor reported as invalid_grant
observation.local: the authority source is an injectable seam (AdapterOptions.authoritySource over kernel/derive.ts's EffectiveAuthoritySource); a source raising SourceUnavailableError maps to temporarily_unavailable/503 with Retry-After (provider.ts sourceUnavailableError plus the header middleware, continuation-grant.ts txError for the custom grants). The tests drive an injected failing source, which is the only way to reach the class here: the local kernel is the authoritative record and can be neither unreachable nor unverifiable to itself, and the rolled-back-version trigger has no external replica to roll back, so the discrimination BETWEEN the three triggers is the source's own duty and stays unobserved

tests.name: transient authority-source failure (@spec issuance-grant#effective-set-projection) > on refresh: refuses temporarily_unavailable (503 + Retry-After) and consumes neither the presented refresh token nor its rotation; the SAME token then succeeds

transient authority-source failure (@spec issuance-grant#effective-set-projection) > at the initial exchange: refuses 503 before the idempotency reservation, so the SAME creation_request_id still redeems
transient authority-source failure (@spec issuance-grant#effective-set-projection) > the permanent class is unaffected: a fully narrowed family still refuses invalid_grant with 400, never 503

requirements.notes: #617 review 1 replaced this rule's invalid_grant mapping: a transient source failure refuses temporarily_unavailable with HTTP 503, so a client tells 'retry this same credential' from 'your authorization is gone' without parsing error_description. Partial rather than tested because the three triggers collapse into one injected signal here; distinguishing them needs the not-yet-built external MAS Mission Status client.

requirements.text: A refresh family's issued authority MUST NOT widen across refreshes within the same Mission: the consuming AS atomically narrows its own stored ceiling on every refresh, or retains the highest Mission state `version` it has observed and rejects a source reporting a lower one as a rollback.

observation.normative: a refresh family's issued authority never widens across a sequence of refreshes spanning multiple containment narrowings within the same Mission: the Mission's state version strictly increases and each refresh's projected remainder is a subset of the previous one, ending in invalid_grant once fully contained
observation.local: the test proves the invariant this single-process kernel guarantees by construction (every refresh re-reads the live, monotonically-narrowing kernel record; there is no external cache or replica that could feed back a stale, wider read), not an actual rollback ATTEMPT against a stale source: that scenario has no constructible case here (same gap as the fail-closed-source row) and would need the not-yet-built issuance-grant external-consuming-AS path to exercise the rollback-rejection half of this rule directly

requirements.notes: No scope-projection mode exists in src for this profile: the demo consuming AS models Mission authority as authorization_details (RFC 9396) throughout and never projects to scope. Todo pending a scope-projection implementation.

observation.normative: a consuming AS incapable of the Effective Authority Set projection (no Mission-state integration, or one that cannot resolve current authorization_details and state version) does not claim containment- or discharge-aware issuance in its conformance statement

requirements.text: the record itself is written atomically with successful issuance, after the state gate and this projection

observation.normative: the single-use record of a redeemed grant is written atomically with successful issuance, after the state gate and the projection, so a redemption that fails before issuance leaves the grant unconsumed and retryable, and two concurrent redemptions of one grant are resolved by that atomic record (the loser is a replay)
observation.local: there is no issuance-grant redemption path in src, so the rule is observed on this implementation's OTHER single-use redemption artifact, the Identity Continuation Assertion: its validator now CHECKS the (iss, jti) and the exchange consumes it at issuance commit through the atomic newReplayCache().recordOnce, whose false is the concurrency loser. The grant-jti half of the rule (and the PAR-carriage variant, where recording at PAR validation IS the atomic step) stays unobserved until a redemption path exists.

requirements.text: the effective authority is the intersection of the verified delegated `authorization_details`, the current entitlement of the mapped origin principal, and current resource and deployment policy. All three are required

observation.normative: both origin-principal-mapping entry points (Cross-Org grant adapter, ID-JAG RAS) consult the mapped local principal's current entitlement unconditionally on every redemption (RAS: base AND continuation grants alike) via the shared EntitlementResolver contract, independently of the static authority-ceiling intersection and of the mapping's own validity bound; a missing, negative, stale-beyond-bound, future-dated, or resolver-exception result each refuse the same way as the other dual-axis failures, and never proceeds as entitled. The observation carries two grains. A bare Boolean is audience-scoped: it authorizes the complete already-intersected authorization_details set for that audience, unmodified. An observation carrying the OPTIONAL authority member is action- and resource-scoped: all three consumers (Cross-Org grant adapter, ID-JAG RAS, PDP) intersect the delegated set with it on exact (resource, action) matching, mint or evaluate the surviving subset when the match is partial, and refuse with the existing non-oracular error only when the intersection is empty, so the quoted text's per-entry intersection is exercised, not only its audience-wide instance

requirements.notes: #539 stage 2: closes the confirmed "no entitlement lookup at all" gap in cross-org-grant.ts and adds the same check to the RAS (previously absent at both entry points). entitlement and entitlementStalenessBoundSeconds are now REQUIRED CrossOrgOptions/RasConfig fields (a compile-time fail-closed guarantee, not a runtime fail-closed-on-unconfigured default): the only construction sites are this test file, services/ras/test/mapping-entitlement.test.ts, src/services/mcp-saas/test/cross-domain.test.ts, src/services/authorization-server/test/continuation-grant.test.ts, and src/demo/src/stack.ts (the live demo wiring), all updated. #744 adds the action- and resource-scoped grain: an OPTIONAL, additive `authority` member on EntitlementObservation carrying the mapped principal's currently entitled (resource, actions) set. Absent, every deployment and every pre-existing row behaves exactly as before (regression-guarded at each consumer). Present, mission-core's shared narrowToEntitledAuthority intersects it with the delegated set per action on exact resource matching (no wildcard or prefix form), and all three consumers carry the surviving subset forward: the Cross-Org adapter mints it and records it as output_authority (no evidence schema change), the RAS mints it on base and continuation grants alike, and the PDP folds the (audience, action) check into entitlementCurrent. Only an empty intersection refuses, with the same non-oracular errors as before (invalid_grant at the RAS and Cross-Org, principal_mapping_failed at the PDP); no new denial reason. Kept partial for one narrower remaining reason: the RAS mints from the grant with no local-ceiling or deployment-policy intersection at all, so the quoted clause's third bound is demonstrated at the Cross-Org adapter (localCeiling) and the PDP (policy view and FGA) but not at that entry point. The audience-wide caveat that previously held this row partial no longer applies.

requirements.text: is closed for `mission-approval-context-v1`. Adding, removing, or redefining a member, or changing how `submission_evidence_commitment` is constructed, MUST use a new `typ`, never a silent reinterpretation of this one

observation.normative: A change to the manifest's member set, a member's meaning, or the submission_evidence_commitment construction is published under a new typ value; mission-approval-context-v1 always denotes exactly the v1 member set this document defines.

tests.name: Approval Context Commitment verification (approval-governance § approval-context-computation) > vector 6: rejects a value committed under a different typ

requirements.text: Reusing the issuance profile's commitment mechanisms supplies canonicalization and algorithm identification and agility. It supplies nothing else

observation.normative: The Default Commitment Construction reused by this profile supplies only canonicalization (JCS, I-JSON) and algorithm identification/agility (the sha-256: prefix and reject-unknown-prefix rule); it supplies no authenticity, approval-time-existence, or selective-disclosure property.

requirements.text: The commitment is an unkeyed digest over Mission Record fields held under the same trust as the record itself. An issuer that can rewrite the record can recompute a matching commitment; authentication comes entirely from the signature of whichever artifact discloses the commitment, never from the digest construction

observation.normative: A bare approval_context_commitment proves nothing an attacker who controls the Mission Record cannot reproduce; whatever authenticates a disclosed commitment is the signature of the artifact carrying it (a Consent Evidence object, an Approval Governance Record, or a future Mandate claim), never the digest itself.

requirements.text: A matching commitment shows the disclosed facts are internally consistent with the retained record. It does not show the facts were true, or that an approval occurred, at the time claimed

observation.normative: A verifier that confirms a matching approval_context_commitment has confirmed internal consistency with the retained record only, never that the recorded approval genuinely occurred at the claimed instant.

requirements.text: The commitment is a flat digest over the complete manifest object; proving anything about one member requires disclosing the whole object

observation.normative: There is no mechanism to prove one manifest member (for example, subject) without disclosing every other member of the same manifest.

requirements.text: `approval_context_commitment` MAY appear as a signed member of an artifact that already authenticates a reference to the Mission

observation.normative: A companion artifact that already authenticates a reference to the Mission (for example, a Consent Evidence object) may add approval_context_commitment as an OPTIONAL signed member, and an introspection response may disclose it to a caller holding the existing member-scoped disclosure privilege that already gates proposal_hash.

requirements.text: `approval_context_commitment` MUST NOT be carried on a Mission-bound access token's baseline `mission` claim

observation.normative: approval_context_commitment never appears on a Mission-bound access token's baseline mission claim, and never on another credential-bound Mission descriptor a companion profile mints for correlation (for example, the Mission Authority Server's Join Assertion): each such descriptor keeps to its own already-fixed minimal member set.

tests.name: Approval Context Commitment carriage (@spec approval-governance#approval-context-carriage, #699) > is never carried on a Mission-bound access token's baseline mission claim

requirements.notes: #699 exercises the baseline-claim half only: the kernel's missionClaim is asserted to be exactly {id, issuer}. The descriptor half (a companion-minted credential-bound Mission descriptor, for example the MAS Join Assertion) has no minting path in this implementation, which resolves the MAS Join from a propagated reference at the PDP, so it stays unexercised and coverage stays partial.
